messages.subject: Population estimate error
parts:
Hi there

I have gathered and assembled some data, and with the help of Distance I am trying to ascertain the population estimate of a species of antelope in a wildlife conservancy in Kenya. I have run my data through the Distance analysis software, but my population estimate arrives at a grand total of 9 for the plains habitat....this is obviously incorrect. So far I have followed very concise and specific instructions on how to run the data through Distance, and I cannot see where the error lies within my data. Additionally, the bar chart outputs also look slightly odd and I'm not sure how to rectify this either. Below, I will attach my data set. Any help would be greatly appreciated. Many thanks

Kind regards

David

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Population estimate error
parts:
David

Thanks for sending along the data.  It required a bit of wrangling before it could be brought into Distance.  Distance expects data to be sorted first by stratum, then by transect within stratum.

So I performed that sorting and brought data for both strata into a single file; with resulting data structure in Distance as

I note each stratum has only 4 transects (challenging to make inference with this many transects).  I also note that each stratum has a transect named Rekero that is 140km in length.

All that notwithstanding, when analysing the data, truncating the 5% most-distant observations, a half-normal provides a reasonable fit (some heaping and lots of detections at distances <10m) to the plains data.

I get an abundance estimate quite different from the "9" animals you achieved

You'll want to do much more assessment and fitting than this.  The sorted data file is attached.  If you have further questions, let us know.
